title: CDE platforms share the federated model with stakeholders but vary sharply in API openness
content:
A Common Data Environment (CDE) is used for sharing 3D models and directly associated data with all stakeholders. What lives there is the **federated model**: discipline-specific part models — structural engineering (load-bearing design), MEPF (mechanical, electricity, plumbing, fire safety), ventilation/HVAC — broken up as required by the BEP and combined in the CDE for **collision detection and management**, a core BIM activity (01:13:06). Deep collision analysis is typically done by architects and engineers, not BIM management (01:14:28).

The platform landscape (BIM briefing + DT BAU walkthrough):
- **Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC)**, now the Autodesk Forma family
- **Dalux** — Danish, closed-source, limited API; explicitly called out as difficult to integrate because it is a closed system (00:07:31)
- **Catenda** — open API but lacking some richer features
- **Squirrel** — another entrant

Openness is the integration bottleneck: closed CDEs restrict custom agents and software (02:05:54), which is precisely the gap a local-first, integrable platform can exploit. Data sovereignty adds another axis: tools can be prohibited when technology or hosting is not EU-based — e.g. Autodesk Forma on some projects (01:38:41).
description: Common Data Environments host the federated BIM model (discipline models + collision checks). ACC/Forma, Dalux, Catenda, Squirrel differ in openness — closed CDEs resist integration.
